video_title: Carmelo and Rasheed Wallace React to the Greatest Comeback in NBA Finals History

quotes.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
quotes.summary_phrase: Carmelo Anthony on the Knicks' historic comeback against the Spurs
quotes.excerpt: I've seen a lot of basketball before. I've never seen no shit like this before.
quotes.quote: I've seen a lot of basketball before. I've never seen no shit like this before. Like, finals on the road, Game 4. We can tie this up and we got a chance to win this shit now. We getting the driver's seat. We up 30 comfortably.

quotes.speaker: Rasheed Wallace
quotes.summary_phrase: Rasheed Wallace on the importance of defensive intensity
quotes.excerpt: If I see you hitting shots and we not hitting no shots, no, let's slow this down.
quotes.quote: If I see you hitting shots and we not hitting no shots, no, let's slow this down. I got the foul, you know. I ain't trying to hurt you, I ain't trying to eat no flagrant, but you won't feel my presence. You got to go to the line, out of bounds or something. I got to slow this momentum up that y'all on.

quotes.speaker: Kazeem Famuyide
quotes.summary_phrase: Kazeem Famuyide on the Knicks' young core and lack of a closer
quotes.excerpt: They're super talented, but they're super young. They don't have a closer.
quotes.quote: They're super talented, but they're super young. Outside of OG Anunoby, they don't have a closer. And you see like the optics, the first two plays, Jalen Brunson in foul trouble. A couple plays down, Jalen Brunson hits a turnaround on the mid. He said, 'I'm in your head, I'm in your head.' Takes the foul on the arm and the neck, says 'I'm in your head' again. It was shaping up to be one of them nights where it's like, 'All right, here's the next superstar that's going to come into the Garden and have his moment and take over.'

quotes.speaker: Rasheed Wallace
quotes.summary_phrase: Rasheed Wallace on the Spurs' failure to utilize Victor Wembanyama
quotes.excerpt: It seemed like San Antonio didn't take advantage of all of his ability.
quotes.quote: To me, it seemed like San Antonio didn't take advantage of all of his ability. You know, they just let him stand out there and jack them threes up. Like, 'All right, young fella, you can shoot the B74, I'm going to give you that.'

quotes.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
quotes.summary_phrase: Carmelo Anthony's assessment of Victor Wembanyama's fatigue
quotes.excerpt: I think he got tired. That's the big thing to me. I think he got tired.
quotes.quote: I think he got tired. That's the big thing to me. I think he got tired. He played the whole fourth quarter in Game 3, and he had the energy. Because even if you go back to the Western Conference series, he would get to his numbers because he's Wembanyama. But if you watch them, if he had a great game, the next game he looked like he was in mud.

quotes.speaker: Rasheed Wallace
quotes.summary_phrase: Rasheed Wallace on the importance of veteran experience in closing games
quotes.excerpt: Experience. That's where it comes in the play at. You got to play your vet.
quotes.quote: Experience. That's where it comes in the play at. You got to play your vet. You got to play HB. Black Falcon need to be out there on that floor. And you're not looking at him as a scorer, but as you said, he's the one that calms everything down for them.

quotes.speaker: Rasheed Wallace
quotes.summary_phrase: Rasheed Wallace on his regret over a specific play against the Spurs
quotes.excerpt: I did a blunderhead move myself against those same damn Spurs.
quotes.quote: I did a blunderhead move myself against those same damn Spurs. We playing in the Palace, and so it was a sideline out of bounds play, and Robert Horry taking the ball out. I'm on the ball, he throws it into the coffin corner to Manu, and something instinctively was like, 'Oh, let's trap this motherfucker.' I go over, I try to trap him, Manu jumps out of bounds and just kicks it right back to Big Shot Bob and the rest is history.

quotes.speaker: Monica McNutt
quotes.summary_phrase: Monica McNutt on the Knicks' expectations in clutch situations
quotes.excerpt: The Knicks have the expectation to perform in clutch. The Spurs are nervous in clutch.
quotes.quote: The Knicks have the expectation to perform in clutch. The Spurs are nervous in clutch because they haven't been able to do it. Twice now in this series the game was in their hands and they haven't been able to do it, and so it becomes a little bit of a self-fulfilling prophecy.

quotes.speaker: Rasheed Wallace
quotes.summary_phrase: Rasheed Wallace on the importance of film study for coaches
quotes.excerpt: I'm going to show all our first quarters. That's our film session.
quotes.quote: I'm going to show all our first quarters. That's our film session. That's when we did a lot of good things. That's when we had big leads in that first half. I'm going to show that. We know what we did on that bad end, and I'm going to show that a little bit of that. That's going to be first, like, 'All right, just what we messed up at, let's block out more, this or that.' But for the rest of that film session, for, you know, that shootaround and the previous practice, yo, it's going to be everything we did good.

quotes.speaker: Rasheed Wallace
quotes.summary_phrase: Rasheed Wallace on the pride of defending home court
quotes.excerpt: It's a sense of pride to defend home court, or to go into someone else's house.
quotes.quote: It goes along with pride and becoming that maven of your craft. Knowing the history, knowing what you're fighting for. I'm trying to get my name up in the rafters too. I ain't just out here just to get the bread. It's a sense of pride to defend home court, or to go into someone else's house and whoop them up. Like what the Knicks did the first two games, me personally, oh, I loved it because that's the type of stuff I like, going to somebody else's crib and we putting hands on you.
